reg.ke-dpa.req.7: Restrict cross-border transfers to countries with adequate protection
reg.ke-dpa.penalties: Administrative fines up to KES 5,000,000 or 1% of annual turnover, whichever is lower. Criminal penalties include fines up to KES 3,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years. Enforced by the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC).
reg.kr-ai-basic-act.name: Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of Trust (AI Basic Act)
reg.kr-ai-basic-act.summary: South Korea's comprehensive national AI regulatory framework, the second after the EU AI Act. Establishes a legal framework for advancing competitiveness in AI while ensuring ethical standards and public trust. Assigns transparency and safety responsibilities to businesses developing or deploying high-impact AI and generative AI.
reg.kr-ai-basic-act.req.1: Notify users when interacting with high-impact AI or generative AI systems
reg.kr-ai-basic-act.req.3: Implement risk management throughout the AI lifecycle with human oversight
reg.kr-ai-basic-act.req.4: Conduct impact assessments on fundamental rights for high-impact AI
reg.kr-ai-basic-act.req.5: Designate a domestic representative for foreign AI providers meeting scale thresholds
reg.kr-ai-basic-act.req.6: Document safety measures for high-impact AI systems
reg.kr-ai-basic-act.req.7: Establish AI safety institute and national AI governance body
reg.kr-ai-basic-act.penalties: Administrative fines up to KRW 30 million (~USD 22,000) for violations of notification obligations, domestic agent designation, and non-compliance with suspension or corrective orders.
reg.kr-ai-framework.name: South Korea AI Basic Act (Framework Act on AI Industry Promotion)
reg.kr-ai-framework.summary: South Korea's AI Basic Act is one of the first comprehensive national AI laws globally. It establishes a regulatory framework promoting AI industry development while managing risks from high-impact AI systems. The law creates the AI Committee under the Prime Minister, mandates impact assessments for high-impact AI, and sets transparency and reliability requirements.
reg.kr-ai-framework.req.1: AI Committee established under the Prime Minister for national AI policy coordination
reg.kr-ai-framework.req.2: High-impact AI designation for systems affecting life, safety, and fundamental rights
reg.kr-ai-framework.req.3: AI impact assessments required for high-impact AI systems before deployment
reg.kr-ai-framework.req.4: Transparency obligations including disclosure of AI-generated content and AI interaction
reg.kr-ai-framework.req.5: AI reliability standards and certification framework
reg.kr-ai-framework.req.6: Support measures for AI industry development, research, and talent cultivation
reg.kr-ai-framework.req.7: User protection measures including right to explanation of AI-driven decisions
reg.kr-ai-framework.penalties: Fines up to KRW 30 million for failure to comply with high-impact AI obligations. Administrative corrective orders and improvement directives. The AI Committee coordinates enforcement across sector-specific regulators.
reg.kr-ncia.name: South Korea National Cybersecurity Infrastructure Act
reg.kr-ncia.summary: South Korea's National Cybersecurity Infrastructure Act establishes a comprehensive legal framework for protecting national cybersecurity across public and private sectors. It consolidates previously fragmented cybersecurity regulations, creates the National Cybersecurity Committee, and mandates incident response coordination between government agencies and critical infrastructure operators.
reg.kr-ncia.req.1: National Cybersecurity Committee established under the President for policy coordination
reg.kr-ncia.req.2: Mandatory cybersecurity incident reporting to the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA)
reg.kr-ncia.req.3: Critical infrastructure operators must implement cybersecurity management systems
reg.kr-ncia.req.4: National cybersecurity strategy development and implementation oversight
reg.kr-ncia.req.5: Cross-sector information sharing on cyber threats and vulnerabilities
reg.kr-ncia.req.6: Regular cybersecurity assessments and compliance audits for designated entities
reg.kr-ncia.penalties: Administrative corrective measures and improvement orders for non-compliant entities. Fines for failure to report cybersecurity incidents. Sector-specific penalties applied through implementing regulations.
reg.kr-pipa.name: Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA)
reg.kr-pipa.summary: South Korea's comprehensive data protection law, substantially amended in September 2023. PIPA regulates all personal information processing in both public and private sectors and is considered one of the strictest privacy laws globally, with revenue-based penalties and data portability rights.
reg.kr-pipa.req.1: Obtain informed consent for collection, use, and third-party provision of personal information
reg.kr-pipa.req.2: Report data breaches to the PIPC and affected individuals within 72 hours
reg.kr-pipa.req.3: Conduct privacy impact assessments for public sector data processing
reg.kr-pipa.req.4: Appoint a Chief Privacy Officer (CPO) meeting qualification requirements
reg.kr-pipa.req.5: Right to data portability and right to refuse automated decision-making
reg.kr-pipa.req.6: Implement technical, physical, and administrative safeguards for personal data
reg.kr-pipa.penalties: Administrative penalties up to 3% of total relevant revenue. Criminal penalties: up to 5 years imprisonment and/or KRW 50 million fine (~USD 37,000). Enforced by the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC).
reg.kz-pdp.name: Kazakhstan Law on Personal Data and Their Protection
reg.kz-pdp.summary: Kazakhstan's Law on Personal Data and Their Protection establishes the legal framework for processing personal data in Kazakhstan. It sets requirements for consent, data security, and cross-border transfers, and designates the Ministry of Digital Development as the supervisory authority overseeing compliance.
reg.kz-pdp.req.1: Consent required for collection and processing of personal data
reg.kz-pdp.req.2: Data subjects' rights to access, correction, supplementation, and blocking of personal data
reg.kz-pdp.req.3: Data localization: databases containing personal data of Kazakh citizens must be located in Kazakhstan
reg.kz-pdp.req.4: Cross-border data transfers permitted only to countries with adequate protection levels
reg.kz-pdp.req.5: Notification to the authorized body before commencing personal data processing
reg.kz-pdp.req.6: Mandatory data security measures including protection against unauthorized access, destruction, and modification
reg.kz-pdp.penalties: Administrative fines for violations of personal data protection requirements. The Ministry of Digital Development may conduct inspections, issue compliance orders, and suspend data processing. Criminal penalties for unlawful collection or dissemination of personal data.
reg.mx-lfpdppp.name: Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (LFPDPPP)
reg.mx-lfpdppp.summary: Mexico's reformed federal data protection law, published March 2025, replaces the original 2010 LFPDPPP. It maintains ARCO rights (Access, Rectification, Cancellation, Opposition), incorporates data minimization and proactive accountability, and transfers enforcement from the dissolved INAI to the Secretariat of Anti-Corruption and Good Governance.
reg.mx-lfpdppp.req.1: Provide a comprehensive privacy notice (aviso de privacidad) before processing
reg.mx-lfpdppp.req.2: Obtain consent (express consent required for sensitive and financial data)
reg.mx-lfpdppp.req.3: Respect ARCO rights (Access, Rectification, Cancellation, Opposition)
reg.mx-lfpdppp.req.4: Implement administrative, technical, and physical security measures
reg.mx-lfpdppp.req.5: Execute data processing agreements with data processors
reg.mx-lfpdppp.req.6: Restrict cross-border transfers to adequate jurisdictions or with consent
reg.mx-lfpdppp.req.7: Designate a person or department responsible for data protection
reg.mx-lfpdppp.penalties: Administrative fines range from 100 to 320,000 UMA. Criminal sanctions of 3 months to 5 years imprisonment for security breaches and deceitful processing. Enforced by the Secretariat of Anti-Corruption and Good Governance.
reg.my-csa.name: Malaysia Cyber Security Act 2024 (Act 854)
reg.my-csa.summary: Malaysia's Cyber Security Act 2024 establishes a comprehensive legal framework for national cybersecurity, designating the National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA) as the lead agency. It mandates cybersecurity measures for National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII) entities across 11 sectors and introduces licensing requirements for cybersecurity service providers.
reg.my-csa.req.1: Designation of National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII) entities across 11 sectors
reg.my-csa.req.2: NCII entities must implement cybersecurity risk assessment and management measures
reg.my-csa.req.3: Mandatory cybersecurity incident reporting to NACSA within prescribed timeframes
reg.my-csa.req.4: Cybersecurity audits and compliance assessments for NCII entities
reg.my-csa.req.5: Licensing framework for cybersecurity service providers
reg.my-csa.req.6: Chief Executive responsibility for ensuring organizational cybersecurity compliance
reg.my-csa.penalties: Fines up to MYR 500,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years for non-compliance with NCII obligations. Additional fines up to MYR 200,000 for failure to report cybersecurity incidents. Continuing offences carry daily penalties of up to MYR 10,000.
reg.my-pdpa.name: Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709, as amended 2024)
reg.my-pdpa.summary: Malaysia's comprehensive personal data protection law governing the processing of personal data in commercial transactions. Significantly amended in 2024 with enhanced penalties effective April 2025, including mandatory breach notification and increased fines.
reg.my-pdpa.req.1: Comply with seven Personal Data Protection Principles (General, Notice and Choice, Disclosure, Security, Retention, Data Integrity, Access)
reg.my-pdpa.req.2: Obtain consent for processing personal data with clear and informed notice
reg.my-pdpa.req.3: Register as a data processor with the Commissioner for specified classes of data users
reg.my-pdpa.req.4: Mandatory data breach notification to the Commissioner and affected individuals
reg.my-pdpa.req.5: Appoint a data protection officer for certain categories of data users
reg.my-pdpa.req.6: Restrictions on cross-border data transfers unless the destination has adequate protections
reg.my-pdpa.req.7: Provide data subjects with access to and correction of their personal data
reg.my-pdpa.penalties: Non-compliance with data protection principles: fines up to MYR 1,000,000 (~USD 210,000) and/or up to 3 years imprisonment. Breach notification violations: up to MYR 250,000 and/or 2 years imprisonment. Unlawful collection or sale of data: up to MYR 500,000 and/or 3 years imprisonment. Enforced by the Department of Personal Data Protection (JPDP).
reg.ng-ncps.name: Nigeria National Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy 2021
reg.ng-ncps.summary: Nigeria's National Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy provides the comprehensive framework for securing Nigeria's cyberspace and digital economy. It establishes the National Cybersecurity Coordination Centre under the Office of the National Security Adviser and mandates cybersecurity measures for critical national information infrastructure across government and private sectors.
reg.ng-ncps.req.1: National Cybersecurity Coordination Centre for policy implementation and threat coordination
reg.ng-ncps.req.2: Critical National Information Infrastructure (CNII) protection across designated sectors
reg.ng-ncps.req.3: Mandatory cybersecurity incident reporting to ngCERT (Nigerian Computer Emergency Response Team)
reg.ng-ncps.req.4: Cybersecurity standards and compliance framework for government agencies and CNII operators
reg.ng-ncps.req.5: Capacity building and cybersecurity workforce development initiatives
reg.ng-ncps.req.6: Public-private partnerships for cybersecurity information sharing and threat intelligence
reg.ng-ncps.penalties: Enforcement through the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act 2015. Penalties for cybercrimes range from fines of NGN 2 million to NGN 7 million and imprisonment of 3 to 7 years. Critical infrastructure attacks carry enhanced penalties.
reg.ng-ndpa.name: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (NDPA)
reg.ng-ndpa.summary: Nigeria's first comprehensive data protection statute replaces the earlier Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR) of 2019. It establishes the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) as a standalone regulatory body and provides a legal framework for the processing of personal data by public and private entities.
reg.ng-ndpa.req.1: Obtain informed, specific, freely given, and unambiguous consent
reg.ng-ndpa.req.2: Execute data processing agreements with all data processors
reg.ng-ndpa.req.3: Conduct data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing
reg.ng-ndpa.req.4: Appoint a Data Protection Officer where required
reg.ng-ndpa.req.5: Register with the NDPC as a data controller of major importance (if applicable)
reg.ng-ndpa.req.6: Implement appropriate technical and organizational security measures
reg.ng-ndpa.req.7: Notify the NDPC of data breaches within 72 hours
reg.ng-ndpa.penalties: Data controllers of major importance: fines up to NGN 10 million or 2% of annual gross revenue, whichever is higher. Other organizations: fines up to NGN 2 million or 2% of annual gross revenue. Enforced by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC).
reg.nz-ncsc.name: New Zealand Intelligence and Security Act 2017 (NCSC Mandate)
reg.nz-ncsc.summary: New Zealand's cybersecurity framework operates through the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) established under the Intelligence and Security Act 2017 within the Government Communications Security Bureau (GCSB). The NCSC provides cybersecurity services to significant government and critical infrastructure organizations, conducting threat detection, incident response, and resilience advisory services.
reg.nz-ncsc.req.1: NCSC provides cyber threat detection and disruption services for organizations of national significance
reg.nz-ncsc.req.2: Cybersecurity incident response and advisory services for government and critical infrastructure
reg.nz-ncsc.req.3: Threat intelligence sharing with Five Eyes partners and domestic stakeholders
reg.nz-ncsc.req.4: Protective cybersecurity assessments for government agencies and critical infrastructure operators
reg.nz-ncsc.req.5: CERT NZ coordinates cybersecurity incident reporting and public awareness
reg.nz-ncsc.req.6: Voluntary cybersecurity frameworks and guidelines for private sector adoption
reg.nz-ncsc.penalties: The framework is primarily advisory and service-based rather than punitive. Government agencies must comply with GCSB protective security requirements. Non-compliance by government entities addressed through public sector accountability mechanisms. Criminal penalties under the Crimes Act 1961 apply to cybercrimes.
reg.nz-privacy-act.name: Privacy Act 2020
reg.nz-privacy-act.summary: New Zealand's updated privacy legislation replacing the Privacy Act 1993. It establishes 13 Information Privacy Principles governing how agencies collect, store, use, and disclose personal information, with mandatory breach notification and extraterritorial application to overseas agencies carrying on business in New Zealand.
reg.nz-privacy-act.req.1: Comply with 13 Information Privacy Principles covering collection, storage, access, and disclosure
reg.nz-privacy-act.req.2: Mandatory notification to the Privacy Commissioner and affected individuals for notifiable privacy breaches
reg.nz-privacy-act.req.3: Provide individuals with access to their personal information upon request
reg.nz-privacy-act.req.4: Only collect personal information that is necessary for a lawful purpose
reg.nz-privacy-act.req.5: Take reasonable steps to ensure personal information is accurate, complete, and not misleading
reg.nz-privacy-act.req.6: Ensure personal information is protected by reasonable security safeguards
reg.nz-privacy-act.penalties: Criminal offence for failure to comply with compliance notices or for misleading an agency: fines up to NZD 10,000. The Human Rights Review Tribunal can award compensatory and other damages with no statutory cap. Enforced by the Office of the Privacy Commissioner (OPC).
reg.pe-ai-law31814.name: Law No. 31814 - Law that Promotes the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Favor of Economic and Social Development
reg.pe-ai-law31814.summary: Peru's foundational AI law establishing a national framework to promote AI development while protecting fundamental rights. Designates the Presidency of the Council of Ministers as the national AI regulator and sets principles for risk-based governance, transparency, and interoperability.
reg.pe-ai-law31814.req.1: Perform risk assessments for AI systems
reg.pe-ai-law31814.req.2: Establish governance structures for AI lifecycle management
reg.pe-ai-law31814.req.3: Ensure transparency and human oversight in AI deployment
reg.pe-ai-law31814.req.4: Guard personal data in AI processing
reg.pe-ai-law31814.req.5: Prohibit unacceptable-risk AI including subliminal manipulation, social scoring, and biometric identification without safeguards
reg.pe-ai-law31814.req.6: Monitor regulatory updates and maintain compliance
reg.pe-ai-law31814.req.7: Cybersecurity and audit requirements per implementing regulation
reg.pe-ai-law31814.penalties: Specific penalty amounts defined by the regulatory authority under implementing regulation (Supreme Decree No. 115-2025-PCM).
reg.pe-law29733.name: Law 29.733 on the Protection of Personal Data
reg.pe-law29733.summary: Peru's data protection law was enacted in 2011 with implementing regulations effective May 2013. A major update via Supreme Decree 016-2024-JUS took effect March 2025, modernizing obligations including extraterritorial application and local representative requirements for foreign entities.
reg.pe-law29733.req.1: Obtain free, prior, express, informed, and unequivocal consent
reg.pe-law29733.req.2: Register personal data banks with the national registry
reg.pe-law29733.req.3: Implement appropriate technical and organizational security measures
reg.pe-law29733.req.4: Respect data subject rights (access, rectification, cancellation, opposition)
reg.pe-law29733.req.5: Restrict cross-border transfers to countries with adequate protection or with consent
reg.pe-law29733.req.6: Appoint a local representative for foreign entities
reg.pe-law29733.req.7: Comply with purpose limitation, proportionality, and data quality principles
reg.pe-law29733.penalties: Minor infractions: up to 5 UIT (~USD 5,500). Serious infractions: up to 50 UIT (~USD 55,000). Very serious infractions: up to 100 UIT (~USD 110,000). Enforced by the Autoridad Nacional de Proteccion de Datos Personales (ANPDP) within the Ministry of Justice.
reg.ph-dpa.name: Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173)
reg.ph-dpa.summary: The Philippines' comprehensive data privacy law establishing rights of data subjects and obligations of personal information controllers and processors. It created the National Privacy Commission as an independent regulatory body and imposes both criminal and administrative penalties for violations.
reg.ph-dpa.req.1: Obtain consent for processing of personal and sensitive personal information
reg.ph-dpa.req.2: Register data processing systems with the National Privacy Commission
reg.ph-dpa.req.4: Mandatory breach notification to the NPC within 72 hours of discovery
reg.ph-dpa.req.5: Implement reasonable and appropriate organizational, physical, and technical security measures
reg.ph-dpa.req.6: Data subject rights including access, correction, erasure, and data portability
reg.ph-dpa.req.7: Comply with requirements for cross-border data transfers including contractual protections
reg.ph-dpa.penalties: Criminal penalties: imprisonment from 1 to 7 years and fines from PHP 500,000 to PHP 5,000,000 (~USD 9,000 to USD 90,000). Penalties increased if the offender is a public official or if the breach affects at least 100 individuals. Enforced by the National Privacy Commission (NPC).
reg.pk-popa.name: Pakistan Personal Data Protection Act
reg.pk-popa.summary: Pakistan's Personal Data Protection Act establishes the country's first comprehensive data privacy framework. It regulates the processing of personal data by public and private entities, introduces consent requirements, creates the National Commission for Personal Data Protection, and sets rules for cross-border data transfers.
reg.pk-popa.req.1: Lawful basis for processing including consent, contractual necessity, and legitimate interest
reg.pk-popa.req.2: Data subject rights including access, rectification, erasure, and data portability
reg.pk-popa.req.3: Data Protection Impact Assessments for high-risk processing activities
reg.pk-popa.req.4: Cross-border data transfer restrictions with government-approved adequacy list
reg.pk-popa.req.5: National Commission for Personal Data Protection as supervisory authority
reg.pk-popa.req.6: Data breach notification to the Commission and affected individuals
reg.pk-popa.penalties: Fines up to PKR 25 million for data controllers and processors. Additional penalties for repeat violations. The National Commission may issue compliance orders, conduct investigations, and impose administrative sanctions.
reg.qa-pdpl.name: Qatar Personal Data Privacy Law (Law No. 13 of 2016)
reg.qa-pdpl.summary: Qatar's Personal Data Privacy Law establishes comprehensive data protection requirements for organizations processing personal data within Qatar, including the Qatar Financial Centre. It mandates consent-based processing, data minimization, and cross-border transfer restrictions, with enforcement by the Compliance and Data Protection Department.
reg.qa-pdpl.req.1: Explicit consent required for collection and processing of personal data
reg.qa-pdpl.req.2: Data minimization and purpose limitation principles
reg.qa-pdpl.req.3: Cross-border data transfer restrictions requiring adequate protection or consent
reg.qa-pdpl.req.4: Data processor agreements with mandatory security and confidentiality provisions
reg.qa-pdpl.req.5: Individual rights to access, rectification, and objection to processing
reg.qa-pdpl.req.6: Special protections for sensitive personal data including health, biometric, and genetic data
reg.qa-pdpl.penalties: Fines up to QAR 5 million for non-compliance. Imprisonment of up to 3 years for serious violations including unauthorized disclosure of personal data. Additional penalties for cross-border transfer violations.
reg.rs-lpdp.name: Law on Personal Data Protection (Zakon o zastiti podataka o licnosti)
reg.rs-lpdp.summary: Serbia's GDPR-aligned data protection law was enacted as part of the country's EU accession process. It incorporates core GDPR principles including data protection by design, data portability, 72-hour breach notification, and mandatory data protection officers.
reg.rs-lpdp.req.1: Implement data protection by design and by default
reg.rs-lpdp.req.2: Conduct data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing
reg.rs-lpdp.req.3: Notify the Commissioner of data breaches within 72 hours
reg.rs-lpdp.req.4: Appoint a data protection officer where required
reg.rs-lpdp.req.5: Ensure lawful basis for processing (consent, contract, legal obligation, etc.)
reg.rs-lpdp.req.6: Respect data subject rights including portability and erasure
reg.rs-lpdp.penalties: Fines for legal entities range from RSD 50,000 to RSD 2,000,000 per violation (~EUR 17,000 maximum). Entrepreneurs face RSD 20,000 to RSD 500,000. Enforced by the Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection.
reg.rw-dpp.name: Law No. 058/2021 Relating to the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy
reg.rw-dpp.summary: Rwanda's data protection law regulates the processing of personal data of individuals in Rwanda by both domestic and foreign entities. It included a 24-month compliance period with enforcement beginning from October 2023, requiring data processor registration, DPO appointment, and breach notification.
reg.rw-dpp.req.1: Register with the NCSA and obtain a Data Protection and Privacy certificate
reg.rw-dpp.req.2: Designate a Data Protection Officer (internal or external)
reg.rw-dpp.req.3: Obtain consent before processing personal data
reg.rw-dpp.req.4: Implement appropriate technical and organizational security measures
reg.rw-dpp.req.5: Notify the authority of data breaches within 48 hours
reg.rw-dpp.req.6: Conduct data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing
reg.rw-dpp.req.7: Restrict cross-border transfers to countries with adequate protection
reg.rw-dpp.penalties: Administrative fines from RWF 2,000,000 to RWF 5,000,000 or 1% of global turnover. Criminal penalties for serious violations: 7-10 years imprisonment and fines of RWF 20,000,000-25,000,000. Enforced by the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA).
reg.sa-nca.name: Saudi Arabia National Cybersecurity Authority Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC)
reg.sa-nca.summary: Saudi Arabia's Essential Cybersecurity Controls are mandatory standards issued by the National Cybersecurity Authority (NCA) applicable to all government entities, government-affiliated organizations, and private sector entities that operate national critical infrastructure. The ECC provides 114 cybersecurity controls across five domains aligned with Saudi Vision 2030.
reg.sa-nca.req.1: Cybersecurity governance: policies, roles, responsibilities, and risk management framework
reg.sa-nca.req.2: Cybersecurity defense: network security, application security, and endpoint protection
reg.sa-nca.req.3: Cybersecurity resilience: business continuity, disaster recovery, and incident management
reg.sa-nca.req.4: Third-party and cloud cybersecurity: vendor risk management and cloud service security
reg.sa-nca.req.5: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) cybersecurity for critical infrastructure operators
reg.sa-nca.req.6: Regular compliance assessments and reporting to the National Cybersecurity Authority
reg.sa-nca.penalties: Non-compliance may result in NCA-directed corrective actions, suspension of government contracts, and regulatory sanctions. Critical infrastructure operators face escalated enforcement including operational restrictions. The NCA may conduct audits and mandate remediation timelines.
reg.sa-pdpl.name: Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree M/19 of 2021, amended 2023)
reg.sa-pdpl.summary: Saudi Arabia's comprehensive data protection framework governing the collection, processing, disclosure, and retention of personal data. Originally issued in 2021 and amended in March 2023, it applies to both public and private sector entities processing personal data within Saudi Arabia.
reg.sa-pdpl.req.1: Obtain consent before collecting or processing personal data
reg.sa-pdpl.req.2: Implement appropriate technical and organizational security measures
reg.sa-pdpl.req.3: Notify SDAIA and affected individuals of data breaches
reg.sa-pdpl.req.5: Conduct data protection impact assessments before high-risk processing
reg.sa-pdpl.req.6: Restrict cross-border transfers to approved jurisdictions or with adequate safeguards
reg.sa-pdpl.req.7: Maintain records of processing activities and privacy policies
reg.sa-pdpl.penalties: Administrative fines up to SAR 5,000,000 (~USD 1.33 million), doubled for repeat offenses. Criminal penalties include imprisonment up to 2 years and/or fine up to SAR 3,000,000 for unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data. Enforced by the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA).
reg.sg-csa.name: Singapore Cybersecurity Act
reg.sg-csa.summary: Singapore's Cybersecurity Act establishes a legal framework for the oversight and maintenance of national cybersecurity. It designates Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) across 11 essential services sectors and empowers the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) to manage cybersecurity threats and incidents.
reg.sg-csa.req.1: Designation of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) across 11 sectors including energy, water, healthcare, and banking
reg.sg-csa.req.2: CII owners must comply with codes of practice and standards of performance
reg.sg-csa.req.3: Mandatory reporting of prescribed cybersecurity incidents to CSA
reg.sg-csa.req.4: Regular cybersecurity audits and risk assessments for CII
reg.sg-csa.req.5: Licensing framework for cybersecurity service providers (penetration testing, managed SOC)
reg.sg-csa.req.6: Commissioner of Cybersecurity empowered to investigate threats and direct emergency measures
reg.sg-csa.penalties: Fines up to SGD 100,000 for failure to comply with CII obligations. Additional fines of up to SGD 50,000 for failure to report cybersecurity incidents. Imprisonment of up to 2 years for providing false information. Continuing offences carry daily penalties.
reg.sg-pdpa.name: Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)
reg.sg-pdpa.summary: Singapore's Personal Data Protection Act governs the collection, use, disclosure, and care of personal data by organizations. It balances individuals' rights to protect their data with organizations' needs to collect and use data for legitimate purposes.
reg.sg-pdpa.req.1: Consent required before collecting, using, or disclosing personal data
reg.sg-pdpa.req.2: Purpose limitation: data used only for purposes the individual was informed of
reg.sg-pdpa.req.3: Access and correction rights for individuals
reg.sg-pdpa.req.5: Data breach notification to PDPC within 3 calendar days of assessment
reg.sg-pdpa.req.6: Mandatory data protection policies and practices
reg.sg-pdpa.req.7: Do Not Call (DNC) Registry compliance for marketing
reg.sg-pdpa.penalties: Up to SGD 1 million or 10% of annual turnover (for organizations with turnover exceeding SGD 10 million).
reg.sg-psa.name: Singapore Payment Services Act (PSA)
reg.sg-psa.summary: The Payment Services Act provides a comprehensive regulatory framework for payment services and digital payment token (cryptocurrency) services in Singapore. Administered by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), it consolidates previously fragmented payment regulations and introduces licensing for digital payment token service providers.
reg.sg-psa.req.1: Three-tier licensing: money-changing, standard payment institution, and major payment institution licenses
reg.sg-psa.req.2: Regulation of seven payment services including digital payment token services and cross-border money transfers
reg.sg-psa.req.3: AML/CFT requirements including customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, and suspicious transaction reporting
reg.sg-psa.req.4: Technology risk management and cybersecurity requirements for payment service providers
reg.sg-psa.req.5: Consumer protection measures including safeguarding of customer funds
reg.sg-psa.req.6: Interoperability requirements for designated payment systems
reg.sg-psa.penalties: Fines up to SGD 250,000 for operating without a license. Additional penalties for AML/CFT violations including imprisonment up to 7 years. MAS may revoke licenses, impose conditions, or issue prohibition orders.
reg.th-csa.name: Thailand Cybersecurity Act B.E. 2562 (2019)
reg.th-csa.summary: Thailand's Cybersecurity Act establishes the National Cybersecurity Committee (NCSC) and a legal framework for preventing, handling, and responding to cybersecurity threats. It designates Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) across government and private sectors and grants authorities emergency powers during severe cyber threats.
reg.th-csa.req.1: National Cybersecurity Committee (NCSC) chaired by the Prime Minister for policy coordination
reg.th-csa.req.2: Designation of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) organizations across key sectors
reg.th-csa.req.3: CII organizations must maintain cybersecurity standards and conduct risk assessments
reg.th-csa.req.4: Mandatory cybersecurity incident reporting to the NCSC
reg.th-csa.req.5: Emergency powers allowing authorities to access computer systems during critical-level cyber threats
reg.th-csa.req.6: Thai-CERT coordination for national incident response and threat intelligence sharing
reg.th-csa.penalties: Fines up to THB 300,000 for CII organizations failing to comply with cybersecurity standards. Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fines up to THB 60,000 for obstructing NCSC operations. Additional penalties for failure to report cybersecurity incidents.
reg.th-pdpa.name: Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019)
reg.th-pdpa.summary: Thailand's comprehensive personal data protection law, enacted in 2019 with full enforcement from 1 June 2022. It governs the collection, use, and disclosure of personal data by data controllers and processors, with provisions closely modeled on the EU GDPR including lawful bases for processing and data subject rights.
reg.th-pdpa.req.1: Obtain consent for collection, use, or disclosure of personal data unless a lawful basis applies
reg.th-pdpa.req.2: Notify data subjects about purposes of data collection before or at the time of collection
reg.th-pdpa.req.3: Implement appropriate security measures to prevent unauthorized access or disclosure
reg.th-pdpa.req.4: Appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) in specified circumstances
reg.th-pdpa.req.5: Data subject rights including access, rectification, erasure, portability, and objection
reg.th-pdpa.req.6: Mandatory data breach notification to the PDPC within 72 hours
reg.th-pdpa.req.7: Restrictions on cross-border data transfers requiring adequate protection
reg.th-pdpa.penalties: Administrative fines up to THB 5 million (~USD 140,000). Criminal penalties up to THB 1 million and/or up to 1 year imprisonment for certain violations. Civil liability for actual damages plus punitive damages up to 2x actual damages. Enforced by the Personal Data Protection Committee (PDPC).
reg.tr-kvkk.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)
reg.tr-kvkk.summary: Turkey's comprehensive data protection law regulates the processing of personal data by both public and private entities, including those outside Turkey handling data of Turkish residents. The law is modeled on EU data protection principles and establishes registration, consent, and security obligations.
reg.tr-kvkk.req.1: Register with the Data Controllers Registry (VERBIS)
reg.tr-kvkk.req.2: Obtain explicit consent for processing sensitive personal data
reg.tr-kvkk.req.3: Implement adequate technical and organizational security measures
reg.tr-kvkk.req.4: Notify the Personal Data Protection Authority of data breaches
reg.tr-kvkk.req.5: Respond to data subject rights requests within 30 days
reg.tr-kvkk.req.6: Ensure cross-border transfers meet adequacy or safeguard requirements
reg.tr-kvkk.req.7: Appoint a data controller representative for foreign entities
reg.tr-kvkk.penalties: Administrative fines range from TRY 68,083 to TRY 13,620,402 (2025 figures, adjusted annually). Criminal penalties of 1-3 years imprisonment for unlawful processing of personal data. Enforced by the Personal Data Protection Authority (KVKK Board).
reg.tz-epda.name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act (Written Laws Amendment Act)
reg.tz-epda.summary: Tanzania's data protection framework was established through amendments to the Electronic and Postal Communications Act and subsequent regulations. It introduces data protection principles, individual rights, and oversight mechanisms for the processing of personal data in Tanzania, with the Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority (TCRA) serving as the supervisory body.
reg.tz-epda.req.1: Consent or other lawful basis required for processing personal data
reg.tz-epda.req.2: Data protection principles including purpose limitation, data minimization, and accuracy
reg.tz-epda.req.3: Individual rights to access, correction, and objection to processing
reg.tz-epda.req.4: Data security obligations including protection against unauthorized access and disclosure
reg.tz-epda.req.5: Cross-border data transfer restrictions requiring adequate safeguards
reg.tz-epda.req.6: Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority (TCRA) oversight and enforcement
reg.tz-epda.penalties: Fines and penalties as prescribed by the Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority. Administrative sanctions including compliance orders and suspension of processing activities. Criminal penalties for serious violations of data protection requirements.
reg.ug-dppa.name: Uganda Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019
reg.ug-dppa.summary: Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act establishes a framework for the protection of personal data, regulates collection and processing by public and private bodies, and creates the Personal Data Protection Office under the National Information Technology Authority. It applies to data controllers and processors operating within Uganda or processing data of Ugandan residents.
reg.ug-dppa.req.1: Registration of data controllers and processors with the Personal Data Protection Office
reg.ug-dppa.req.2: Consent or other specified lawful basis for collection and processing of personal data
reg.ug-dppa.req.3: Data subject rights including access, correction, and deletion
reg.ug-dppa.req.4: Data Protection Impact Assessments for processing likely to result in high risk
reg.ug-dppa.req.5: Cross-border data transfers only with adequate safeguards or consent
reg.ug-dppa.req.6: Mandatory data breach notification to the Personal Data Protection Office
reg.ug-dppa.penalties: Fines up to UGX 4.8 million or imprisonment up to 10 years, or both. Higher penalties for repeat offenders. The Personal Data Protection Office may issue compliance orders and conduct investigations.
reg.us-ca-ai-transparency.name: California AI Transparency Act (SB 942)
reg.us-ca-ai-transparency.summary: Requires large generative AI providers to watermark AI-generated content and provide free detection tools. Focuses on image, video, and audio content transparency. Applies to providers with over 1 million monthly users accessible in California.
reg.us-ca-ai-transparency.req.1: Embed invisible watermarks in AI-generated image, video, and audio content
reg.us-ca-ai-transparency.req.2: Watermarks must include creator name, AI system version, timestamp, and unique identifier
reg.us-ca-ai-transparency.req.3: Provide free, publicly available detection tools for checking AI-generated content
reg.us-ca-ai-transparency.req.4: Offer visible label option that users can choose to include
reg.us-ca-ai-transparency.req.5: Large online platforms must provide content provenance inspection tools
reg.us-ca-ai-transparency.req.6: Does not apply to text-only content
reg.us-ca-ai-transparency.penalties: $5,000 per violation. Each day of non-compliance is a separate offense. Enforced by the California Attorney General, city attorneys, and county counsel.
reg.us-ca-ccpa.name: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CPRA)
reg.us-ca-ccpa.summary: The California Consumer Privacy Act, amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA), grants California residents expanded rights over their personal information. It applies to businesses meeting revenue or data processing thresholds and establishes the California Privacy Protection Agency for enforcement.
reg.us-ca-ccpa.req.1: Right to know what personal information is collected and how it is used
reg.us-ca-ccpa.req.2: Right to delete personal information held by businesses
reg.us-ca-ccpa.req.3: Right to opt-out of the sale or sharing of personal information
reg.us-ca-ccpa.req.4: Right to non-discrimination for exercising privacy rights
reg.us-ca-ccpa.req.5: Right to correct inaccurate personal information (CPRA)
reg.us-ca-ccpa.req.6: Right to limit use of sensitive personal information (CPRA)
reg.us-ca-ccpa.req.7: Mandatory privacy notices at or before the point of collection
reg.us-ca-ccpa.penalties: Up to $7,500 per intentional violation; $2,500 per unintentional violation. Private right of action for data breaches: $100-$750 per consumer per incident.
reg.us-circia.name: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act (CIRCIA)
reg.us-circia.summary: CIRCIA requires critical infrastructure entities to report substantial cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransomware payments within 24 hours. Signed into law in March 2022, CISA's final rulemaking establishes reporting obligations for 16 critical infrastructure sectors defined by Presidential Policy Directive 21.
reg.us-circia.req.1: Report substantial cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours of reasonable belief
reg.us-circia.req.2: Report ransomware payments to CISA within 24 hours
reg.us-circia.req.3: Preserve data relevant to covered cyber incidents for at least two years
reg.us-circia.req.4: Supplemental reports required when substantial new or different information becomes available
reg.us-circia.req.5: Covers 16 critical infrastructure sectors including energy, financial services, healthcare, and communications
reg.us-circia.req.6: CISA may issue subpoenas to non-compliant entities and refer to DOJ
reg.us-circia.penalties: Non-compliance may result in CISA subpoenas, contempt of court proceedings, and referral to the Department of Justice. Entities that fail to comply with subpoenas may face civil action. Reports are protected from use in regulatory enforcement actions.
reg.us-cmmc.name: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification 2.0 (CMMC)
reg.us-cmmc.summary: CMMC 2.0 is a Department of Defense program that requires defense contractors to demonstrate cybersecurity maturity through third-party assessments. It streamlines the original five-level model into three tiers aligned with NIST SP 800-171 and NIST SP 800-172, and will be required in DoD contracts through DFARS clauses.
reg.us-cmmc.req.1: Level 1 (Foundational): 15 basic safeguarding practices from FAR 52.204-21, annual self-assessment
reg.us-cmmc.req.2: Level 2 (Advanced): 110 security requirements from NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2, triennial third-party assessment
reg.us-cmmc.req.3: Level 3 (Expert): NIST SP 800-172 enhanced requirements, government-led assessment
reg.us-cmmc.req.4: Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) allowed for limited deficiencies with 180-day remediation
reg.us-cmmc.req.5: Annual affirmation by senior official of continued compliance
reg.us-cmmc.req.6: Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) flow-down to subcontractors
reg.us-cmmc.penalties: Non-certified contractors are ineligible for DoD contract awards requiring CMMC. False certification may result in False Claims Act liability with treble damages. Suspension or debarment from government contracting for material misrepresentation.
reg.us-co-ai-act.name: Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act (SB 24-205)
reg.us-co-ai-act.summary: The most detailed AI-specific consumer protection law in the United States. Focuses on preventing algorithmic discrimination in consequential decisions covering employment, education, healthcare, housing, insurance, and legal services. Requires a duty of care from both developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems.
reg.us-co-ai-act.req.1: Developers must use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination
reg.us-co-ai-act.req.2: Deployers must implement a risk management policy and program
reg.us-co-ai-act.req.3: Complete impact assessments for high-risk AI systems
reg.us-co-ai-act.req.4: Notify consumers when high-risk AI systems make or substantially factor into consequential decisions
reg.us-co-ai-act.req.5: Provide consumers with right to explanation of AI's role in decisions
reg.us-co-ai-act.req.6: Report known algorithmic discrimination to the Attorney General
reg.us-co-ai-act.req.7: Rebuttable presumption of compliance for those following specified provisions
reg.us-co-ai-act.penalties: $20,000 per violation counted per consumer or transaction. Enforced exclusively by the Colorado Attorney General under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act. No private right of action.
reg.us-co-cpa.name: Colorado Privacy Act (CPA)
reg.us-co-cpa.summary: The Colorado Privacy Act provides Colorado residents with rights over their personal data and establishes obligations for data controllers. It applies to entities conducting business in Colorado or targeting Colorado residents that control or process data of 100,000 or more consumers annually, or 25,000 or more consumers while deriving revenue from the sale of personal data.
reg.us-co-cpa.req.1: Right to access, confirm, and obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-co-cpa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-co-cpa.req.4: Right to opt out of targeted advertising, sale of personal data, and certain profiling
reg.us-co-cpa.req.5: Universal opt-out mechanism recognition required by July 1, 2024
reg.us-co-cpa.req.6: Data protection assessments required for processing that presents heightened risk
reg.us-co-cpa.req.7: Purpose limitation and data minimization obligations for controllers
reg.us-co-cpa.penalties: Enforced by the Colorado Attorney General and district attorneys. Civil penalties up to $20,000 per violation, with a maximum of $500,000 per related series of violations. 60-day cure period, which sunsets on January 1, 2025.
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.name: Connecticut Data Privacy Act (CTDPA)
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.summary: The Connecticut Data Privacy Act provides Connecticut residents with comprehensive rights over their personal data. It applies to entities conducting business in Connecticut or producing products or services targeted at Connecticut residents that control or process data of 100,000 or more consumers, or 25,000 or more consumers while deriving more than 25% of gross revenue from personal data sales.
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.req.1: Right to access, correct, delete, and obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.req.2: Right to opt out of the sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.req.3: Consent required for processing sensitive data
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.req.4: Universal opt-out mechanism recognition required beginning January 1, 2025
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.req.5: Data protection assessments for high-risk processing activities
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.req.6: Clear and accessible privacy notices with specified disclosures
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.req.7: Data minimization and purpose limitation requirements
reg.us-ct-ctdpa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Connecticut Attorney General under the Connecticut Unfair Trade Practices Act. Civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation. 60-day cure period, which sunsets on December 31, 2024.
reg.us-de-dpdpa.name: Delaware Personal Data Privacy Act (DPDPA)
reg.us-de-dpdpa.summary: The Delaware Personal Data Privacy Act grants Delaware residents comprehensive rights over their personal data. It applies to entities conducting business in Delaware or targeting Delaware residents that control or process data of 35,000 or more consumers, or 10,000 or more consumers while deriving more than 20% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data. Delaware's thresholds are among the lowest of any state privacy law, reflecting its smaller population.
reg.us-de-dpdpa.req.1: Right to access, correct, delete, and obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-de-dpdpa.req.2: Right to opt out of the sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-de-dpdpa.req.3: Consent required before processing sensitive personal data
reg.us-de-dpdpa.req.4: Universal opt-out mechanism recognition required beginning January 1, 2026
reg.us-de-dpdpa.req.5: Data protection assessments for processing that presents heightened risk
reg.us-de-dpdpa.req.6: Clear and meaningful privacy notice obligations
reg.us-de-dpdpa.req.7: Data minimization and purpose limitation requirements for controllers
reg.us-de-dpdpa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Delaware Department of Justice. Civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation. 60-day cure period, which sunsets on December 31, 2025. No private right of action.
reg.us-exec-ai.name: US Executive Order on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI (EO 14110)
reg.us-exec-ai.summary: Executive Order 14110 established the most comprehensive US federal AI governance framework, requiring safety testing and reporting for dual-use foundation models, directing federal agencies to develop AI governance policies, and addressing risks from AI in critical infrastructure, cybersecurity, and biological weapons. Note: portions were rescinded by subsequent executive action in January 2025.
reg.us-exec-ai.req.1: Safety testing and red-teaming reporting for dual-use foundation models exceeding compute thresholds
reg.us-exec-ai.req.2: NIST AI Risk Management Framework and AI safety standards development
reg.us-exec-ai.req.3: Federal agency AI governance policies and Chief AI Officer designations
reg.us-exec-ai.req.4: Watermarking and content authentication for AI-generated content
reg.us-exec-ai.req.5: Privacy protections for AI training data and federal data practices
reg.us-exec-ai.req.6: Civil rights protections against AI-enabled discrimination in housing, lending, and employment
reg.us-exec-ai.req.7: Workforce impact assessments and AI talent recruitment for federal government
reg.us-exec-ai.penalties: Compliance is mandatory for federal agencies and contractors through existing regulatory authorities. Dual-use foundation model developers must report safety test results under the Defense Production Act. Non-compliance may result in loss of federal contracts and regulatory action under applicable sector-specific laws.
reg.us-fcpa.name: Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA)
reg.us-fcpa.summary: The Foreign Corrupt Practices Act prohibits US persons and entities from bribing foreign government officials to obtain or retain business. It also requires SEC-registered companies to maintain accurate books and records and adequate internal accounting controls, making it a cornerstone of international anti-corruption enforcement.
reg.us-fcpa.req.1: Anti-bribery provisions: prohibit payments to foreign officials to influence acts or secure improper advantage
reg.us-fcpa.req.2: Books and records provisions: maintain accurate books, records, and accounts in reasonable detail
reg.us-fcpa.req.3: Internal controls: devise and maintain adequate internal accounting controls
reg.us-fcpa.req.4: Third-party due diligence for agents, consultants, and business partners
reg.us-fcpa.req.5: Applies to US issuers, domestic concerns, and foreign nationals acting within US territory
reg.us-fcpa.req.6: No exception for facilitating or grease payments under DOJ enforcement policy
reg.us-fcpa.penalties: Criminal penalties: up to $250,000 and 5 years imprisonment for individuals; up to $2 million per violation for entities. Civil penalties up to $16,000 per violation. Disgorgement of profits, pre-judgment interest, and injunctive relief. DOJ and SEC concurrent enforcement authority.
reg.us-fl-fdbr.name: Florida Digital Bill of Rights (FDBR)
reg.us-fl-fdbr.summary: The Florida Digital Bill of Rights grants data privacy rights to Florida residents and imposes obligations on controllers and processors. It applies to entities conducting business in Florida with gross annual revenues exceeding $1 billion and meeting specific data processing criteria, making it one of the narrowest state privacy laws in scope. It also includes provisions targeting large technology platforms and protections for children.
reg.us-fl-fdbr.req.1: Right to access, correct, delete, and obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-fl-fdbr.req.2: Right to opt out of the sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-fl-fdbr.req.3: Consent required before processing sensitive personal data
reg.us-fl-fdbr.req.4: Enhanced protections for children under 18, including opt-in consent for those under 13
reg.us-fl-fdbr.req.5: Data protection assessments for processing that presents heightened risk to consumers
reg.us-fl-fdbr.req.6: Restrictions on surveillance and data collection by large technology platforms
reg.us-fl-fdbr.req.7: Government entities prohibited from using social media to censor or suppress speech
reg.us-fl-fdbr.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Florida Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation, with treble damages for violations involving children. 45-day cure period for alleged violations. No private right of action.
reg.us-glba.name: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA)
reg.us-glba.summary: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act requires financial institutions to explain their information-sharing practices to customers and to safeguard sensitive data. Its Financial Privacy Rule, Safeguards Rule, and Pretexting provisions establish a framework for protecting nonpublic personal information (NPI) held by financial institutions including banks, securities firms, and insurance companies.
reg.us-glba.req.1: Financial Privacy Rule: clear privacy notices to customers describing data collection and sharing practices
reg.us-glba.req.2: Opt-out rights for consumers before sharing NPI with nonaffiliated third parties
reg.us-glba.req.3: Safeguards Rule: comprehensive information security program with administrative, technical, and physical safeguards
reg.us-glba.req.4: Designated qualified individual to oversee and implement the information security program
reg.us-glba.req.5: Regular risk assessments and testing of security controls
reg.us-glba.req.6: Pretexting provisions: prohibit obtaining customer information through false pretenses
reg.us-glba.req.7: Service provider oversight and contractual security requirements
reg.us-glba.penalties: Financial institutions face fines up to $100,000 per violation. Officers and directors face personal fines up to $10,000 per violation. Imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals. FTC, banking regulators, and state attorneys general enforce compliance.
reg.us-hipaa.name: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
reg.us-hipaa.summary: HIPAA is a US federal law that establishes national standards for the protection of individually identifiable health information. It regulates how healthcare providers, health plans, healthcare clearinghouses, and their business associates handle Protected Health Information (PHI), imposing strict privacy, security, and breach notification requirements.
reg.us-hipaa.scope: Healthcare entities handling Protected Health Information (PHI), including health plans, healthcare clearinghouses, healthcare providers conducting electronic transactions, and their business associates
reg.us-hipaa.req.1: Privacy Rule: limits use and disclosure of PHI without patient authorization
reg.us-hipaa.req.2: Security Rule: administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for electronic PHI
reg.us-hipaa.req.3: Breach Notification Rule: notify affected individuals, HHS, and media (for large breaches) within 60 days
reg.us-hipaa.req.4: Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) required for all third-party PHI handlers
reg.us-hipaa.req.5: Minimum Necessary Standard: limit PHI access to the minimum needed for a given purpose
reg.us-hipaa.req.6: Individual rights to access, amend, and receive an accounting of disclosures of their PHI
reg.us-hipaa.req.7: Administrative requirements including privacy officer designation, workforce training, and sanctions policies
reg.us-hipaa.penalties: Civil penalties range from $100 to $50,000 per violation, up to $1.5 million per year per violation category. Criminal penalties up to $250,000 and 10 years imprisonment for knowing misuse of PHI.
reg.us-ia-icdpa.name: Iowa Consumer Data Protection Act (ICDPA)
reg.us-ia-icdpa.summary: The Iowa Consumer Data Protection Act provides Iowa residents with data privacy rights and imposes obligations on controllers and processors. It applies to entities conducting business in Iowa or targeting Iowa residents that control or process data of 100,000 or more consumers, or 25,000 or more consumers while deriving more than 50% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data. It is considered one of the more business-friendly state privacy laws.
reg.us-ia-icdpa.req.1: Right to access and confirm whether a controller is processing personal data
reg.us-ia-icdpa.req.2: Right to delete personal data provided by the consumer
reg.us-ia-icdpa.req.3: Right to obtain a portable copy of personal data in a readily usable format
reg.us-ia-icdpa.req.4: Right to opt out of the sale of personal data and targeted advertising
reg.us-ia-icdpa.req.5: Consent required before processing sensitive personal data
reg.us-ia-icdpa.req.6: Clear and accessible privacy notice with mandated disclosures
reg.us-ia-icdpa.req.7: Controllers must respond to consumer requests within 90 days
reg.us-ia-icdpa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Iowa Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. 90-day cure period with no sunset provision. No private right of action. No right to correct inaccurate data.
reg.us-il-ai-employment.name: Illinois AI Employment Discrimination Law (HB 3773)
reg.us-il-ai-employment.summary: Amends the Illinois Human Rights Act to address AI use in employment decisions. Prohibits employers from using AI that discriminates against employees based on protected classes and requires notice to employees and applicants when AI is used in employment decisions.
reg.us-il-ai-employment.req.1: Prohibits AI use that discriminates based on protected classes in recruitment, hiring, promotion, discharge, discipline, or terms of employment
reg.us-il-ai-employment.req.2: Employers must provide notice to employees and applicants when AI is used in employment decisions
reg.us-il-ai-employment.req.3: Failure to provide AI notice is a standalone violation of the Human Rights Act
reg.us-il-ai-employment.req.4: Applies to recruitment, hiring, promotion, renewal, training, discharge, discipline, and tenure decisions
reg.us-il-ai-employment.req.5: Employers must maintain compliance with existing nondiscrimination obligations when deploying AI
reg.us-il-ai-employment.penalties: Civil penalties up to $5,000 per willful or repeated violation. Actual damages and attorney's fees. Each affected individual may constitute a separate violation.
reg.us-il-aivra.name: Illinois Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act
reg.us-il-aivra.summary: One of the first AI-specific laws in the United States. Regulates the use of AI analysis in video interviews for employment purposes. Requires employers to notify applicants, explain AI functionality, and obtain consent before using AI to evaluate video interviews.
reg.us-il-aivra.req.1: Notify applicants that AI may be used to analyze video interviews
reg.us-il-aivra.req.2: Provide information explaining how the AI works and what characteristics it evaluates
reg.us-il-aivra.req.3: Obtain applicant's consent before using AI analysis
reg.us-il-aivra.req.4: Prohibit sharing of applicant video interviews except with those whose expertise is necessary for evaluation
reg.us-il-aivra.req.5: Upon request, destroy video interviews within 30 days
reg.us-il-aivra.penalties: Enforced under the Illinois Attorney General's authority. Violators subject to civil penalties determined by enforcement action.
reg.us-in-incdpa.name: Indiana Consumer Data Protection Act
reg.us-in-incdpa.summary: The Indiana Consumer Data Protection Act establishes consumer privacy rights for Indiana residents. It applies to entities conducting business in Indiana or targeting its residents that control or process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 consumers if deriving more than 50% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data.
reg.us-in-incdpa.req.1: Right to confirm whether a controller is processing personal data and to access that data
reg.us-in-incdpa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-in-incdpa.req.3: Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-in-incdpa.req.4: Right to data portability in a readily usable format
reg.us-in-incdpa.req.5: Right to opt out of sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-in-incdpa.req.6: Consent required before processing sensitive data including precise geolocation and biometric data
reg.us-in-incdpa.req.7: Controllers must respond to consumer requests within 45 days with one 45-day extension
reg.us-in-incdpa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Indiana Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. 30-day cure period for violations; no private right of action.
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.name: Kentucky Consumer Data Protection Act
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.summary: The Kentucky Consumer Data Protection Act provides consumer data privacy rights for Kentucky residents. It applies to entities conducting business in Kentucky or targeting its residents that control or process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 consumers if deriving more than 50% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data.
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.req.1: Right to confirm whether a controller is processing personal data and to access that data
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.req.3: Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.req.4: Right to obtain a copy of personal data in a portable and readily usable format
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.req.5: Right to opt out of sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.req.6: Consent required before processing sensitive data such as racial, health, and biometric data
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.req.7: Controllers must conduct data protection assessments for high-risk processing activities
reg.us-ky-kcdpa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Kentucky Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. 30-day cure period for violations; no private right of action.
reg.us-md-modpa.name: Maryland Online Data Privacy Act
reg.us-md-modpa.summary: The Maryland Online Data Privacy Act is one of the most restrictive state privacy laws, imposing strong data minimization requirements and prohibiting the sale of sensitive data entirely. It applies to entities conducting business in Maryland or targeting its residents that control or process personal data of at least 35,000 consumers, or 10,000 consumers if deriving more than 20% of revenue from selling personal data.
reg.us-md-modpa.req.1: Right to confirm whether a controller is processing personal data and to access that data
reg.us-md-modpa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-md-modpa.req.3: Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-md-modpa.req.4: Right to obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-md-modpa.req.5: Right to opt out of sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-md-modpa.req.6: Prohibition on the sale of sensitive data outright, not merely requiring opt-in consent
reg.us-md-modpa.req.7: Strong data minimization requirement limiting collection to what is reasonably necessary
reg.us-md-modpa.penalties: Enforced by the Maryland Attorney General under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. Civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation; up to $25,000 per violation for repeated offenses. No private right of action.
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.name: Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.summary: The Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act provides comprehensive data privacy protections for Minnesota residents. It applies to entities conducting business in Minnesota or targeting its residents that control or process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 consumers if deriving more than 25% of revenue from selling personal data.
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.req.1: Right to access and confirm whether a controller is processing personal data
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.req.3: Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.req.4: Right to data portability in a readily usable format
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.req.5: Right to opt out of sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.req.6: Right to question the results of profiling decisions and be informed of the reason behind them
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.req.7: Data protection assessments required for processing activities that present heightened risk of harm
reg.us-mn-mcdpa.penalties: Enforced by the Minnesota Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. No private right of action. Controllers must honor universal opt-out mechanisms.
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.name: Montana Consumer Data Privacy Act (MTCDPA)
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.summary: The Montana Consumer Data Privacy Act provides Montana residents with rights over their personal data and establishes obligations for data controllers and processors. It applies to entities conducting business in Montana or targeting Montana residents that control or process data of 50,000 or more consumers, or 25,000 or more consumers while deriving more than 25% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data. Montana's lower population threshold reflects its smaller population.
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.req.1: Right to access, correct, delete, and obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.req.2: Right to opt out of the sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.req.3: Consent required before processing sensitive personal data
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.req.4: Universal opt-out mechanism recognition required beginning January 1, 2025
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.req.5: Data protection assessments for processing presenting heightened risk to consumers
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.req.6: Clear and accessible privacy notice with mandated disclosures
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.req.7: Purpose limitation and data minimization obligations for controllers
reg.us-mt-mtcdpa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Montana Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. 60-day cure period, which sunsets on April 1, 2026. No private right of action.
reg.us-ne-ndpa.name: Nebraska Data Privacy Act
reg.us-ne-ndpa.summary: The Nebraska Data Privacy Act provides comprehensive data privacy protections for Nebraska residents. Unlike most state privacy laws, it applies to all entities conducting business in Nebraska that process personal data without a minimum processing threshold, making it one of the broadest state privacy laws in scope.
reg.us-ne-ndpa.req.1: Right to confirm whether a controller is processing personal data and to access that data
reg.us-ne-ndpa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-ne-ndpa.req.3: Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-ne-ndpa.req.4: Right to obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-ne-ndpa.req.5: Right to opt out of sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-ne-ndpa.req.6: Consent required before processing sensitive data including biometric and geolocation data
reg.us-ne-ndpa.req.7: Controllers must provide clear and accessible privacy notices disclosing data practices
reg.us-ne-ndpa.penalties: Enforced by the Nebraska Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. 30-day cure period for violations; no private right of action.
reg.us-nh-nhpa.name: New Hampshire Privacy Act (SB 255)
reg.us-nh-nhpa.summary: The New Hampshire Privacy Act establishes consumer data privacy rights for New Hampshire residents. It applies to entities conducting business in the state or targeting its residents that control or process the personal data of at least 35,000 consumers, or 10,000 consumers if deriving more than 25% of revenue from selling personal data.
reg.us-nh-nhpa.req.1: Right to confirm whether a controller is processing personal data and to access that data
reg.us-nh-nhpa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-nh-nhpa.req.3: Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-nh-nhpa.req.4: Right to data portability in a readily usable format
reg.us-nh-nhpa.req.5: Right to opt out of sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-nh-nhpa.req.6: Requirement to obtain consent before processing sensitive data
reg.us-nh-nhpa.req.7: Controllers must conduct data protection assessments for targeted advertising and sale of personal data
reg.us-nh-nhpa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the New Hampshire Attorney General under the state Consumer Protection Act. Civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation; no private right of action.
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1)
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.summary: The de-facto US federal reference framework for trustworthy AI. Voluntary, non-regulatory guidance published by the National Institute of Standards and Technology under the National AI Initiative Act of 2020. Organized around four core functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) applied iteratively across the AI lifecycle. Complemented by the Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1, published July 2024) and a companion Playbook with actionable practices. Widely cited in US federal procurement, sector-specific guidance, and state AI laws (notably the Colorado AI Act) as the baseline for what constitutes reasonable AI risk management.
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.scope: Voluntary framework applicable to any organization designing, developing, deploying, or evaluating AI systems within the United States or for US users. Especially load-bearing for US federal agencies, contractors, and regulated industries (healthcare, finance, employment) where downstream rules increasingly reference NIST AI RMF as the baseline standard of care.
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.req.1: GOVERN: establish AI risk management policies, accountability structures, and a culture of risk-awareness across the AI lifecycle
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.req.2: MAP: contextualize each AI system — intended use, stakeholders, jurisdictional scope, third-party dependencies, and the risks specific to its deployment context
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.req.3: MEASURE: quantitatively and qualitatively assess identified risks using rigorous methods, with documented metrics for accuracy, robustness, fairness, transparency, security, and privacy
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.req.4: MANAGE: prioritize, treat, and monitor risks — including risk acceptance, mitigation, or system retirement decisions — with documented response plans for adverse events
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.req.5: Apply the Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) for foundation models and generative systems, addressing risks specific to confabulation, dangerous content, data privacy leakage, and information integrity
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.req.6: Maintain documentation traceable across the four functions to support internal audit and external accountability
reg.us-nist-ai-rmf.penalties: Voluntary framework with no statutory penalties. However, adoption is increasingly load-bearing under other laws: failure to implement NIST AI RMF practices can be cited as evidence of negligence under tort law, can disqualify federal contractors under emerging procurement rules, and is referenced as the compliance baseline in the Colorado AI Act and similar state-level statutes.
reg.us-nj-njdpa.name: New Jersey Data Privacy Act
reg.us-nj-njdpa.summary: The New Jersey Data Privacy Act grants New Jersey consumers rights over their personal data and imposes obligations on controllers and processors. It applies to entities conducting business in New Jersey or targeting its residents that process data of at least 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 consumers if deriving revenue from selling personal data.
reg.us-nj-njdpa.req.1: Right to access personal data collected by a controller
reg.us-nj-njdpa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-nj-njdpa.req.3: Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-nj-njdpa.req.4: Right to obtain a copy of personal data in a portable format
reg.us-nj-njdpa.req.5: Right to opt out of the sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-nj-njdpa.req.6: Requirement to conduct data protection assessments for high-risk processing activities
reg.us-nj-njdpa.req.7: Prohibition on processing sensitive data without consumer consent
reg.us-nj-njdpa.penalties: Up to $10,000 per violation for first offenses; up to $20,000 per violation for subsequent offenses. Enforced exclusively by the New Jersey Attorney General; no private right of action.
reg.us-ny-apda.name: New York Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure Act
reg.us-ny-apda.summary: First US state law requiring disclosure of AI-driven personalized pricing. Mandates clear notification when consumer prices are set by algorithms using personal data. Aims to protect consumers from opaque AI-driven price discrimination.
reg.us-ny-apda.req.1: Display clear and conspicuous disclosure alongside algorithmically personalized prices
reg.us-ny-apda.req.2: Disclosure must state that the price was set by an algorithm using the consumer's personal data
reg.us-ny-apda.req.3: Applies to any entity using personal data to set individualized consumer prices
reg.us-ny-apda.req.4: Disclosure must be presented at the point of sale or display of price
reg.us-ny-apda.penalties: Civil penalty up to $1,000 per violation regardless of actual consumer injury.
reg.us-ny-ll144.name: NYC Local Law 144 - Automated Employment Decision Tools
reg.us-ny-ll144.summary: Regulates the use of automated employment decision tools (AEDTs) in hiring and promotion decisions in New York City. Requires independent bias audits, public disclosure of audit results, and candidate notification before using AI-powered hiring tools.
reg.us-ny-ll144.req.1: Conduct independent bias audit of AEDT no more than 1 year prior to use
reg.us-ny-ll144.req.2: Publish summary of bias audit results on employer's website
reg.us-ny-ll144.req.3: Notify candidates that AEDT will be used in hiring or promotion decisions
reg.us-ny-ll144.req.4: Disclose how the AEDT will be used and what data will be collected
reg.us-ny-ll144.req.5: Allow candidates to request alternative selection process or human review
reg.us-ny-ll144.penalties: Civil penalties of up to $500 for first violation and additional violations on the same day. $500 to $1,500 for each subsequent violation. Each day of non-compliance constitutes a separate violation.
reg.us-or-ocpa.name: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act (OCPA)
reg.us-or-ocpa.summary: The Oregon Consumer Privacy Act provides Oregon consumers with comprehensive data privacy rights and applies broadly to entities conducting business in Oregon or targeting Oregon residents. It covers entities that control or process data of 100,000 or more consumers, or 25,000 or more consumers while deriving 25% or more of annual gross revenue from selling personal data. Notably, it extends certain rights to nonprofit organizations, unlike most other state privacy laws.
reg.us-or-ocpa.req.1: Right to access, correct, delete, and obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-or-ocpa.req.2: Right to opt out of the sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-or-ocpa.req.3: Right to obtain a list of third parties to whom data has been disclosed
reg.us-or-ocpa.req.4: Consent required before processing sensitive data including demographic data
reg.us-or-ocpa.req.5: Data protection assessments required for high-risk processing activities
reg.us-or-ocpa.req.6: Applicability to nonprofit organizations beginning July 1, 2025
reg.us-or-ocpa.req.7: Data minimization and purpose limitation obligations for controllers
reg.us-or-ocpa.penalties: Enforced by the Oregon Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. 30-day cure period available until January 1, 2026. No private right of action.
reg.us-pa-padpa.name: Pennsylvania Data Privacy Act
reg.us-pa-padpa.summary: Pennsylvania's Data Privacy Act establishes consumer data privacy rights for one of the largest US state economies. It follows the Virginia/Connecticut framework with rights to access, delete, and opt out of data sales, while imposing data protection assessment requirements and processor-controller contractual obligations.
reg.us-pa-padpa.req.1: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, and obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-pa-padpa.req.2: Right to opt out of sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-pa-padpa.req.3: Data controllers must provide clear and accessible privacy notices
reg.us-pa-padpa.req.4: Data protection assessments required for targeted advertising, sale of data, and sensitive data processing
reg.us-pa-padpa.req.5: Data processing agreements with mandatory security and confidentiality provisions
reg.us-pa-padpa.req.6: Heightened consent requirements for processing sensitive personal data
reg.us-pa-padpa.penalties: Enforcement exclusively by the Pennsylvania Attorney General with civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. No private right of action. 30-day cure period for violations.
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.name: Rhode Island Data Transparency and Privacy Protection Act
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.summary: The Rhode Island Data Transparency and Privacy Protection Act establishes consumer data privacy rights for Rhode Island residents. It applies to entities conducting business in Rhode Island or targeting its residents that control or process personal data of at least 35,000 consumers, or 10,000 consumers if deriving more than 20% of revenue from selling personal data.
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.req.1: Right to confirm whether a controller is processing personal data and to access that data
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.req.3: Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.req.4: Right to obtain a portable copy of personal data in a usable format
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.req.5: Right to opt out of sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.req.6: Consent required before processing sensitive data including biometric and health data
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.req.7: Controllers must maintain reasonable data security practices and provide transparent privacy notices
reg.us-ri-ridtppa.penalties: Enforced by the Rhode Island Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation. No private right of action. Violators may also be subject to injunctive relief.
reg.us-sox.name: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX)
reg.us-sox.summary: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act was enacted in response to major corporate accounting scandals (Enron, WorldCom) to protect investors through improved accuracy and reliability of corporate disclosures. It established the PCAOB, mandated internal control assessments, and imposed criminal penalties for securities fraud and document destruction.
reg.us-sox.req.1: Section 302: CEO and CFO certification of accuracy of financial statements and effectiveness of internal controls
reg.us-sox.req.2: Section 404: Annual assessment of internal controls over financial reporting with external auditor attestation
reg.us-sox.req.3: Section 802: Criminal penalties for altering, destroying, or concealing documents to impede investigations
reg.us-sox.req.4: Section 806: Whistleblower protections for employees reporting securities violations
reg.us-sox.req.5: Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) registration and inspection of audit firms
reg.us-sox.req.6: Audit committee independence requirements and financial expert designation
reg.us-sox.req.7: Real-time disclosure of material changes in financial condition
