reg.us-sox.penalties: Criminal penalties up to $5 million in fines and 20 years imprisonment for securities fraud. Up to $1 million and 10 years for document destruction. Civil penalties including officer and director bars, disgorgement of profits, and shareholder lawsuits.
reg.us-tn-elvis.name: Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security Act (ELVIS Act)
reg.us-tn-elvis.summary: The first US state law specifically protecting individuals from unauthorized AI voice cloning and deepfakes. Expands Tennessee's right of publicity law to explicitly cover voice protection against AI-generated replicas. Applies nationwide regardless of where the individual resides or where the violation occurs.
reg.us-tn-elvis.req.1: Prohibits unauthorized commercial use of an individual's voice including AI-generated replicas
reg.us-tn-elvis.req.2: Creates liability for publishing or distributing AI-generated voice or likeness without authorization
reg.us-tn-elvis.req.3: Creates cause of action against distributors of AI tools whose primary purpose is producing unauthorized replicas
reg.us-tn-elvis.req.4: Protects voice and likeness of deceased persons for up to 12 years after death
reg.us-tn-elvis.req.5: Extends protection regardless of geographic location of individual or violation
reg.us-tn-elvis.penalties: Class A misdemeanor (up to 11 months 29 days jail, up to $2,500 fine). Treble damages for knowing use of unauthorized voice replica. Treble damages plus attorney's fees when victim is armed forces member.
reg.us-tn-tipa.name: Tennessee Information Protection Act
reg.us-tn-tipa.summary: The Tennessee Information Protection Act establishes consumer data privacy rights for Tennessee residents. It applies to entities conducting business in Tennessee or targeting its residents that exceed $25 million in revenue and control or process personal information of at least 25,000 consumers, or derive more than 50% of revenue from selling personal information of at least 175,000 consumers.
reg.us-tn-tipa.req.1: Right to confirm whether a controller is processing personal information and to access that data
reg.us-tn-tipa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal information
reg.us-tn-tipa.req.3: Right to delete personal information provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-tn-tipa.req.4: Right to obtain a copy of personal information in a portable format
reg.us-tn-tipa.req.5: Right to opt out of sale of personal information, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-tn-tipa.req.6: Affirmative defense available for controllers maintaining a privacy program conforming to NIST frameworks
reg.us-tn-tipa.req.7: Consent required before processing sensitive data such as biometric, geolocation, and health data
reg.us-tn-tipa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Tennessee Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. 60-day cure period for violations; no private right of action.
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.name: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act (TDPSA)
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.summary: The Texas Data Privacy and Security Act provides Texas residents with data privacy rights and imposes obligations on businesses that process personal data. Notably, the TDPSA has no revenue or data volume threshold, applying to any entity conducting business in Texas or producing products or services consumed by Texas residents that processes personal data, excluding small businesses as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration.
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.req.1: Right to access, correct, delete, and obtain a portable copy of personal data
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.req.2: Right to opt out of the sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.req.3: Consent required for processing sensitive personal data
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.req.4: Data protection assessments required for high-risk processing activities
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.req.5: Clear and accessible privacy notice requirements
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.req.6: Universal opt-out mechanism recognition required beginning January 1, 2025
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.req.7: Data processing agreements required between controllers and processors
reg.us-tx-tdpsa.penalties: Enforced by the Texas Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. 30-day cure period for alleged violations. No private right of action.
reg.us-tx-traiga.name: Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (TRAIGA, HB 149)
reg.us-tx-traiga.summary: Texas's first comprehensive AI law. Focuses on prohibiting AI systems designed for harmful purposes rather than broad regulatory compliance. Requires disclosure by state agencies and healthcare providers. Provides affirmative defenses for NIST AI Risk Management Framework compliance.
reg.us-tx-traiga.req.1: Prohibits AI systems intended to incite self-harm or criminal activity
reg.us-tx-traiga.req.2: Prohibits AI for generating child sexual abuse material or deepfake pornography
reg.us-tx-traiga.req.3: Prohibits government use of AI for social scoring
reg.us-tx-traiga.req.4: State agencies must disclose AI interactions to consumers
reg.us-tx-traiga.req.5: Healthcare providers must disclose AI use in treatment to patients
reg.us-tx-traiga.req.6: Affirmative defense available for compliance with NIST AI Risk Management Framework
reg.us-tx-traiga.req.7: 60-day cure period after receiving notice of violation from the Attorney General
reg.us-tx-traiga.penalties: Curable violations: $10,000 to $12,000 per violation. Uncurable violations: $80,000 to $200,000 per violation. Continuing violations: $2,000 to $40,000 per day. Plus attorney's fees and court costs.
reg.us-ut-aipa.name: Utah Artificial Intelligence Policy Act (SB 149)
reg.us-ut-aipa.summary: One of the first comprehensive state AI consumer protection laws in the US. Brings generative AI usage into Utah's consumer protection framework. Requires disclosure of AI interactions in licensed and regulated professions and establishes the Office of AI Policy.
reg.us-ut-aipa.req.1: Disclose use of generative AI when providing services requiring a license or state certification
reg.us-ut-aipa.req.2: Disclose AI interaction to any person who directly asks whether they are interacting with AI
reg.us-ut-aipa.req.3: Businesses are liable for consumer deception caused by their AI systems
reg.us-ut-aipa.req.4: Licensed mental health providers must disclose AI use upfront
reg.us-ut-aipa.req.5: Establish Office of AI Policy within consumer protection division
reg.us-ut-aipa.req.6: AI Learning Lab Program to study risks and benefits
reg.us-ut-aipa.penalties: Administrative fine up to $2,500. Civil penalty up to $5,000. Criminal liability if AI is used to commit an offense.
reg.us-ut-ucpa.name: Utah Consumer Privacy Act (UCPA)
reg.us-ut-ucpa.summary: The Utah Consumer Privacy Act establishes consumer data privacy rights for Utah residents and applies to data controllers and processors conducting business in Utah. It is considered more business-friendly than other state privacy laws, with higher applicability thresholds requiring annual revenue of $25 million or more, and either controlling or processing data of 100,000 or more consumers or deriving over 50% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data of 25,000 or more consumers.
reg.us-ut-ucpa.req.1: Right to access and confirm whether a controller is processing personal data
reg.us-ut-ucpa.req.2: Right to delete personal data provided by the consumer to the controller
reg.us-ut-ucpa.req.3: Right to obtain a portable copy of personal data in a readily usable format
reg.us-ut-ucpa.req.4: Right to opt out of the sale of personal data or targeted advertising
reg.us-ut-ucpa.req.5: Consent required before processing sensitive data
reg.us-ut-ucpa.req.6: Clear and conspicuous privacy notice with specified content requirements
reg.us-ut-ucpa.req.7: Controllers must establish and respond to consumer requests within 45 days
reg.us-ut-ucpa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Utah Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. 30-day cure period with no sunset provision. No private right of action.
reg.us-va-vcdpa.name: Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act (VCDPA)
reg.us-va-vcdpa.summary: The Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act grants Virginia consumers rights over their personal data and imposes obligations on data controllers and processors. It applies to entities that conduct business in Virginia or target Virginia residents and process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 consumers while deriving over 50% of gross revenue from data sales.
reg.us-va-vcdpa.req.1: Right to access personal data held by a controller
reg.us-va-vcdpa.req.2: Right to correct inaccuracies in personal data
reg.us-va-vcdpa.req.3: Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer
reg.us-va-vcdpa.req.4: Right to obtain a portable copy of personal data in a usable format
reg.us-va-vcdpa.req.5: Right to opt out of processing for targeted advertising, sale, or profiling
reg.us-va-vcdpa.req.6: Data protection assessments required for high-risk processing activities
reg.us-va-vcdpa.req.7: Contracts required between controllers and processors governing data handling
reg.us-va-vcdpa.penalties: Enforced exclusively by the Virginia Attorney General. Civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. No private right of action. 30-day cure period for alleged violations.
reg.us-vt-dpa.name: Vermont Data Privacy Act (H.121)
reg.us-vt-dpa.summary: Vermont's Data Privacy Act provides comprehensive consumer data privacy rights with notably stronger provisions than most US state privacy laws. It includes a private right of action for consumers, data broker registration requirements building on Vermont's existing data broker law, and strong protections against profiling and automated decision-making.
reg.us-vt-dpa.req.1: Consumer rights to access, delete, correct, and port personal data
reg.us-vt-dpa.req.2: Right to opt out of sale, targeted advertising, and automated profiling
reg.us-vt-dpa.req.3: Private right of action allowing consumers to sue for violations
reg.us-vt-dpa.req.4: Data broker registration and transparency requirements
reg.us-vt-dpa.req.5: Data Protection Impact Assessments for high-risk processing activities
reg.us-vt-dpa.req.6: Heightened protections for sensitive data including biometric and health information
reg.us-vt-dpa.penalties: Enforcement by the Vermont Attorney General. Private right of action with statutory damages. Civil penalties for data broker registration violations. No cure period for consumer-initiated enforcement.
reg.us-wi-wdpa.name: Wisconsin Data Privacy Act
reg.us-wi-wdpa.summary: Wisconsin's Data Privacy Act establishes consumer data privacy rights following the Virginia/Connecticut model. It provides residents with rights to access, delete, correct, and opt out of the sale of personal data and targeted advertising, with obligations on data controllers and processors operating in Wisconsin.
reg.us-wi-wdpa.req.1: Consumer rights to access, delete, correct, and obtain a copy of personal data
reg.us-wi-wdpa.req.2: Right to opt out of sale of personal data, targeted advertising, and profiling
reg.us-wi-wdpa.req.3: Data controller obligations including privacy notices, purpose limitation, and data minimization
reg.us-wi-wdpa.req.4: Data protection assessments for targeted advertising, sale of data, and profiling activities
reg.us-wi-wdpa.req.5: Data processing agreements required between controllers and processors
reg.us-wi-wdpa.req.6: 30-day cure period for violations before enforcement action
reg.us-wi-wdpa.penalties: Enforcement by the Wisconsin Attorney General with civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. No private right of action. 30-day cure period allows businesses to remedy violations before penalties apply.
reg.uy-law18331.name: Law 18.331 on the Protection of Personal Data and Habeas Data Action (LPDP)
reg.uy-law18331.summary: Uruguay's comprehensive data protection law was one of the earliest in Latin America, earning an EU adequacy determination in 2012. It establishes principles for the processing of personal data, creates a regulatory authority, and grants data subjects habeas data rights.
reg.uy-law18331.req.1: Obtain prior, express, and informed consent for data processing
reg.uy-law18331.req.2: Register all databases with the URCDP
reg.uy-law18331.req.3: Implement appropriate technical and organizational security measures
reg.uy-law18331.req.4: Ensure data quality, accuracy, and relevance
reg.uy-law18331.req.5: Respect data subject rights (access, rectification, inclusion, suppression)
reg.uy-law18331.req.6: Restrict cross-border transfers to countries with adequate protection
reg.uy-law18331.req.7: Comply with purpose limitation and proportionality principles
reg.uy-law18331.penalties: Administrative sanctions include warnings, fines up to 500,000 indexed units (~USD 65,000), suspension of the database for up to 5 business days, or cancellation of the database. Enforced by the Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales (URCDP).
reg.uz-pdp.name: Uzbekistan Law on Personal Data
reg.uz-pdp.summary: Uzbekistan's Law on Personal Data establishes a framework for the protection of personal information in Central Asia's most populous country. It regulates the collection, processing, storage, and transfer of personal data, with oversight by a designated state authority. The law applies to automated and manual processing by government and private entities.
reg.uz-pdp.req.1: Consent required for collection and processing of personal data with specified exceptions
reg.uz-pdp.req.2: Purpose limitation and data minimization principles
reg.uz-pdp.req.3: Individual rights to access, correction, and deletion of personal data
reg.uz-pdp.req.4: Data localization: personal data of Uzbek citizens must be stored on servers within Uzbekistan
reg.uz-pdp.req.5: Cross-border data transfers subject to government approval or bilateral agreements
reg.uz-pdp.req.6: Registration of personal data databases with the authorized state body
reg.uz-pdp.penalties: Administrative fines for violations of personal data processing rules. Criminal liability for unlawful collection, storage, or dissemination of personal data. The authorized state body may issue compliance orders and suspend data processing activities.
reg.vn-pdpl.name: Law on Personal Data Protection (Law No. 91/2025/QH15)
reg.vn-pdpl.summary: Vietnam's comprehensive personal data protection law, passed June 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, replacing the earlier Decree 13/2023. It governs personal data processing activities by domestic and foreign entities handling Vietnamese citizens' data, with data localization requirements and revenue-based penalties.
reg.vn-pdpl.req.1: Obtain consent for personal data processing with specific form and content requirements
reg.vn-pdpl.req.2: Mandatory data breach notification within 72 hours to the Department of Cybersecurity
reg.vn-pdpl.req.3: Conduct impact assessments for cross-border data transfers and file with authorities
reg.vn-pdpl.req.4: Appoint a data protection department or officer for organizations processing large volumes of data
reg.vn-pdpl.req.5: Data subject rights including access, correction, deletion, and withdrawal of consent
reg.vn-pdpl.req.6: Data localization requirements with copies of data stored in Vietnam for cross-border transfers
reg.vn-pdpl.req.7: Register and declare data processing activities with the Ministry of Public Security
reg.vn-pdpl.penalties: For sale or purchase of personal data: fines of 10x revenue from the sale or VND 3 billion (~USD 120,000), whichever is higher. For cross-border transfer violations: 5% of prior year's revenue or VND 3 billion. Enforced by the Department of Cybersecurity and High-Tech Crime Prevention under the Ministry of Public Security.
reg.za-popia.name: Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA), Act 4 of 2013
reg.za-popia.summary: South Africa's comprehensive data protection law regulates the processing of personal information by public and private bodies. It commenced on 1 July 2020 with a one-year grace period, making enforcement effective from 1 July 2021. POPIA grants data subjects extensive rights similar to the GDPR.
reg.za-popia.req.1: Process personal information only with a lawful justification (consent, contract, legal obligation, etc.)
reg.za-popia.req.2: Implement adequate security safeguards to protect personal information
reg.za-popia.req.3: Notify the Information Regulator and data subjects of security compromises
reg.za-popia.req.4: Appoint an Information Officer and register with the Information Regulator
reg.za-popia.req.5: Conduct impact assessments for high-risk processing activities
reg.za-popia.req.6: Restrict cross-border transfers to countries with adequate protection
reg.za-popia.req.7: Ensure purpose limitation, minimality, and data quality
reg.za-popia.penalties: Administrative fines of up to ZAR 10 million or 10% of annual turnover, whichever is higher. Criminal penalties include up to 10 years imprisonment for serious offenses. Enforced by the Information Regulator (South Africa).
